description: Total min/max primitives over signed i64 values. The contracts assert both the order property (result <= a && result <= b for min, result >= a && result >= b for max) and the membership property (result is one of the inputs). Proven with Z3 integer theory only. The generated file MUST begin with a header comment block (// ======) identifying the module as 'std/math/min_max — verified min/max primitives'. Comments must be in Japanese to match the surrounding std style. Each atom follows the convention used in std/math/clamp.mm: `atom name(params) requires: ...; ensures: ...; body: { ... };`. Do NOT invent new operators, types, or syntax — use only what std/core.mm and std/math/clamp.mm already use (conditional expressions, comparisons).

atoms.name: min2
atoms.description: Minimum of two i64 values. The contract proves both the order property and that the result is one of the inputs.
atoms.ensures: result <= a && result <= b && (result == a || result == b)

atoms.name: max2
atoms.description: Maximum of two i64 values. The contract proves both the order property and that the result is one of the inputs.
atoms.ensures: result >= a && result >= b && (result == a || result == b)

atoms.name: min3
atoms.description: Minimum of three i64 values. Z3 discharges the contract by case-splitting on two ordered comparisons.
atoms.ensures: result <= a && result <= b && result <= c && (result == a || result == b || result == c)
